category: rotating residential, static residential and mobile proxy
tier: Residential Proxies (per GB) and Static Residential (per IP)

free_tier.stated: No free tier stated on the plan pages. The home page lists residential from $0.33/GB, mobile from $1.61/GB, unlimited residential from $7.91/hour, datacenter from $0.6/IP and static residential from $1/IP, and offers a free web-proxy page.
free_tier.notes: A second landing page lists different from-prices (residential $0.35/GB, mobile $3.2/GB, datacenter $1/IP, static $1.9/IP), so the from-prices vary by page.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an address or a traffic quota, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a proxy session or a rented address, not stored bytes

egress.terms: Residential is per GB ('Never Expires' on the home-page tile); static residential is 'Per-IP pricing, no traffic fees'.

interface_detail: HTTP(S) and SOCKS5; API and username and password extraction; targeting by country, city, state, zip code, coordinates and ASN on the residential line.
tooling: Any client that speaks an HTTP(S) or SOCKS5 proxy with a username and password or an allowlisted source address: curl -x, python requests, rclone --socks5, or a host-side hop for a runtime that cannot dial a proxy itself.
chaining: A host-side hop dials the vendor's HTTP(S) or SOCKS5 endpoint with credentials; the upstream sees an address from the vendor's pool in place of the caller's address.

limits.value: residential from $0.33/GB (home page), $0.35/GB (second landing page); static residential from $1/IP, no traffic fees

limits_note: The pool figure (90M+ residential IPs, 190+ countries) is a vendor claim. The pool is described as 'sourced from carefully selected partners', so supply comes from third-party partners, not from the vendor's own networks.
binding_note: Residential traffic is metered per GB; the static line is per IP with unlimited traffic.

identity_cost.detail: The login page says 'Unverified emails will be auto-registered upon verification', with Google sign-in as an alternative, so an email and its verification code open the account; no phone, card or identity document is asked at that step. Payment methods are shown as icons and were not readable.

reliability_note: /pricing answers a bot challenge to a page reader and /register returns no content; the static price page is readable through a second reader. unverified: the registration class of the exits (rung 5): no address was looked up.
confidence_note: Prices and the sign-up behaviour are from the vendor's pages; the pool and ISP labels are vendor claims.
